AIP-C01 Task 1.5 Exam Notes: Retrieval Mechanisms

How exam questions on Task 1.5 are worded, which answer wins, and why the others lose. Task 1.5, post 7 of 7.

[IMAGE: cover-1-5-exam.png — alt: "Task 1.5 exam notes"]

AIP-C01 Hands-on Labs · Domain 1 · Task 1.5: Design retrieval mechanisms for FM augmentation · Post 7 of 7. Exam notes for the whole task.

The six previous posts explained each skill in Task 1.5. This one is for exam preparation: how questions on this task are worded, which answer wins, and why the other options lose. Read it after the skill posts, and again in the week before your exam.

Task 1.5 on one page

Task 1.5: Design retrieval mechanisms for FM augmentation has six skills. Here's the core idea of each, and the words in a question that should make you think of it:

[IMAGE: t1-5-summary.png — alt: "Task 1.5 summary: core idea and trigger words for skills 1.5.1 to 1.5.6"]

How to read a Task 1.5 question

  1. Locate the failure in the pipeline. Chunk → embed → store → search → rerank → query handling → access. The symptom tells you the stage: missing context is chunking, missing part numbers is search, wrong order is reranking, informal wording is the query.
  2. Fix that stage, not a later one. A reranker can't recover a passage that was never retrieved; a bigger model can't fix a bad chunk.
  3. Prefer the built-in option. Knowledge Bases chunking strategies, hybrid search, reranking and query decomposition beat custom code when they fit.

Skill 1.5.1: Chunking

[IMAGE: t1-5-1-exam.png — alt: "Exam scenarios for chunking: hierarchical, semantic, no chunking, page numbers, transformation Lambda, new data source"]

Traps: making fixed chunks bigger to recover context; choosing no chunking when citations need page numbers; editing the chunking of an existing data source (you can't).

Covered in post 1: Skill 1.5.1: Chunking Documents for Better Retrieval (lab).

Skill 1.5.2: Embedding models

[IMAGE: t1-5-2-exam.png — alt: "Exam scenarios for embeddings: fewer dimensions, multimodal, multilingual, batch inference, re-embedding, golden set evaluation"]

Traps: a bigger model when the goal is lower storage; text embeddings for images; synchronous calls for tens of millions of records; upgrading the model without re-embedding the corpus.

Covered in post 2: Skill 1.5.2: Choose and Use Embedding Models (lab).

Skill 1.5.3: Deploying vector search

[IMAGE: t1-5-3-exam.png — alt: "Exam scenarios for deploying vector search: quick create, pgvector, knn_vector dimension, OpenSearch Serverless, data access policy"]

Traps: changing the embedding model to fit an index (fix the index dimension instead); granting IAM permissions and forgetting the OpenSearch Serverless data access policy; managed domains when “no nodes to manage” is asked.

Covered in post 3: Skill 1.5.3: Deploy Vector Search: OpenSearch, pgvector or Knowledge Bases.

Skill 1.5.4: Hybrid search and reranking

[IMAGE: t1-5-4-exam.png — alt: "Exam scenarios for hybrid search and reranking: part numbers, reranker, rank fusion, HYBRID search type, recall first"]

Traps: fine-tuning embeddings to find product codes; raising numberOfResults instead of reranking; adding raw keyword and vector scores; expecting a reranker to fix missing passages.

Covered in post 4: Skill 1.5.4: Hybrid Search and Reranking (lab).

Skill 1.5.5: Query handling

[IMAGE: t1-5-5-exam.png — alt: "Exam scenarios for query handling: expansion, decomposition, Step Functions with Map, built-in decomposition, conversational rewrite"]

Traps: a new embedding model for informal wording; one search for a multi-part question; one long Lambda function where the question asks for retries and visibility; searching a follow-up question without its history.

Covered in post 5: Skill 1.5.5: Rewrite Queries for Better Retrieval (lab).

Skill 1.5.6: Access mechanisms

[IMAGE: t1-5-6-exam.png — alt: "Exam scenarios for access mechanisms: function calling, MCP server, API Gateway and Lambda, AgentCore Gateway, tool-call loops"]

Traps: retrieving on every request when the model should decide; separate integrations per app instead of one MCP server; giving other teams direct access to the vector store; raising max tokens to stop a tool loop.

Covered in post 6: Skill 1.5.6: Give Models a Standard Way to Search (lab).

Keyword shortcuts for Task 1.5

  • “Answers lack surrounding context” → hierarchical chunking
  • “No headings, topics shift” → semantic chunking
  • “Custom splitting logic” → Lambda custom transformation
  • “Reduce vector storage” → Titan V2 at 512 or 256 dimensions, tested on recall
  • “Search images and text together” → Titan Multimodal Embeddings
  • “Embed millions of records cheaply” → Bedrock batch inference
  • “Vectors plus SQL joins” → Aurora PostgreSQL + pgvector
  • “Part numbers, exact names not found” → hybrid search
  • “Right passage, wrong position” → reranker model
  • “Informal questions, formal documents” → query expansion
  • “Several questions in one” → query decomposition
  • “Model decides when to search” → function calling
  • “Many AI clients, one search” → MCP server
